answer: Forging 100 aliases therefore burns 63 bonds held for 5 days each, plus the vertex attestations those aliases can never earn. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so an attacker cannot recover it by rotating identities. Each identity must lock a bond, called an anchor, before it can post or attest. A single sonnet checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
